description_full: VeriSign, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides internet infrastructure and domain name registry services that enable internet navigation for various recognized domain names worldwide. The company provides root zone maintainer services operating two of thirteen internet root servers; and registration services and authoritative resolution for the .com and .net domains, which support global e-commerce. It also operates directory for .name and .cc; and back-end systems for .edu domain names. The company was incorporated in 1995 and is headquartered in Reston, Virginia.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 926 people. Revenue per employee of $1.8M ranks in the top quartile among Technology peers. Each employee generates $1.2M of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $75K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 1× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (4/10).
financial_summary: VeriSign, Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $28.1B market cap on $1.7B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years and +5% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +2.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

The business throws off $1.1B in free cash flow — roughly 64 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.32× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 15× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 3.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 11% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
